stemMd:
In the eight months after the regional tourism board launched a multilingual website, overnight stays by foreign visitors in the region's hotels rose by 9 percent. The board concludes that the website attracted additional foreign visitors to the region.

Which of the following, if true, most strengthens the board's conclusion?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Over the same eight months, overnight stays by foreign visitors in a neighbouring region with a similar climate and similar prices, which launched no new website, did not change.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The website is available in five languages, one more than the website of the neighbouring region.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Overnight stays by domestic visitors in the region also rose by about 9 percent over the same eight months.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Most foreign visitors who stayed in the region's hotels had booked through travel agencies rather than online.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The tourism board employs three people who work exclusively on the website.

explanationMd:
The board moves from "the number rose after the launch" to "the launch caused the rise". The weak point is that something else may have raised the number in the same months: a strong season, a favourable exchange rate, a general recovery in travel. The strongest supporting evidence is therefore a **comparison** that rules such causes out.

A neighbouring region with a similar climate and similar prices offers exactly that. It shared the same conditions but did not launch a website, and its foreign stays did not change. If the general conditions had lifted foreign visits, that region would have risen too. This makes the website a much better explanation of the regional rise.

The other choices either point toward a general upswing (domestic visitors also rising), suggest the website was not how visitors booked (travel agencies), or say nothing about cause at all (number of languages, size of the web team).

distractorRationale.c: This weakens the conclusion. A rise of the same size among domestic visitors, who are not the target of a multilingual website, suggests a general upswing that would explain the foreign increase without the website.
distractorRationale.b: A comparison of the number of languages says nothing about whether visitors came because of the site. It gives no evidence that the website changed anyone's decision.
distractorRationale.d: This weakens the conclusion, because it suggests that the website was not how most foreign visitors found or chose the region.
distractorRationale.e: Staffing shows the board takes the website seriously, not that it changed the number of visitors.

accessibilityText: An argument question about strengthening a conclusion. A regional tourism board says overnight stays by foreign visitors rose by 9 percent in the eight months after it launched a multilingual website, and concludes that the website attracted additional foreign visitors. The question asks which statement most strengthens that conclusion. The choices: domestic overnight stays also rose about 9 percent; the site has one more language than the neighbouring region's; most foreign visitors booked through travel agencies; three staff work only on the site; a similar neighbouring region without a new website saw no change in foreign stays.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank. Scenario, names and figures are invented; no published TOLC or other test item was used or adapted.

review.author: tolc-e-wave6-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: A gives a matched control region with no new website and no change, which rules out a general trend and strengthens the causal claim. C suggests a region-wide rise unrelated to foreign-language outreach, so it weakens. D weakens. B and E are irrelevant. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tolce-logic-run5) reached the same answer: A gives a comparable control region with no new website and no change in foreign stays, which rules out a general trend. C weakens, because it points to a region-wide factor. D weakens too, since most bookings did not go online. B and E are irrelevant.]

review.notes: Uniqueness check: only the control-region comparison supplies evidence that the rise is not due to general conditions. Two of the distractors weaken the conclusion and two are irrelevant. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
